climate_pressure: Heat, drought, seasonal drying, and soil-moisture stress affecting agriculture
documented_impact: Higher rainfed-cropland exposure, yield variability, livestock stress, and irrigation demand
fcv_mediator: War-damaged assets, mines, land-access restrictions, input and logistics disruption, displacement, and limited adaptation finance
possible_consequence: Climate pressures may deepen rural livelihood and food-system losses in war-affected areas, but warfare and markets remain independent primary drivers
alternative_explanations: Military damage, occupation, mines, input prices, trade disruption, farm policy, and labour shortages can reduce production without a climate shock.
uncertainty: Climate exposure and war damage are separately documented, but their joint contribution to observed production is not estimated.
compact_statement: Heat and drought may deepen agricultural losses where war has damaged irrigation, assets, access, logistics, and adaptive capacity.

climate_pressure: Severe seasonal cold and future heat requiring reliable electricity, heating, water, health, and housing systems
documented_impact: Heating, power, water, health, and school disruption during energy attacks and cold exposure
fcv_mediator: Targeted infrastructure destruction, centralized-system dependence, repair constraints, poverty, disability, and high-rise building design
possible_consequence: Weather exposure produces larger and more unequal health and service losses when warfare disables interconnected infrastructure
alternative_explanations: Infrastructure age, maintenance, poverty, and centralized design can create outages and unequal service access without warfare or climate change.
uncertainty: The observed cold-war interaction is direct, but cold is not attributed to climate change and future heat interactions are inferential.
compact_statement: War-damaged energy systems can convert severe weather into cascading and unequal heating, water, health, and education failures.

climate_pressure: Drought, changing seasonal water availability, flood risk, and future water scarcity
documented_impact: Higher agricultural, drinking-water, ecosystem, and irrigation demand under damaged and altered hydrological systems
fcv_mediator: Destroyed water infrastructure, Kakhovka reservoir loss, power dependence, contamination, mines, occupation, and restricted monitoring
possible_consequence: Conflict damage can reduce water-system flexibility and magnify future drought or flood losses across southern and eastern Ukraine
alternative_explanations: Pre-war infrastructure condition, water policy, abstraction, land use, and ordinary hydrological variability also determine water-system performance.
uncertainty: War impacts are observed, but the additional effect on future climate losses and specific reconstruction alternatives is not quantified.
compact_statement: War damage to water and irrigation systems can magnify drought and flood vulnerability by reducing flexibility, access, monitoring, and ecosystem functions.

climate_pressure: Hotter, drier fire weather and drought affecting forests, farms, and protected areas
documented_impact: Higher background ignition and spread conditions, burned landscapes, air pollution, and ecosystem damage
fcv_mediator: Military ignition sources, unexploded ordnance, access restrictions, degraded monitoring, and constrained fire suppression
possible_consequence: Wildfires may become more frequent, larger, or harder to control where climate fire weather and hostilities overlap
alternative_explanations: Land management, agricultural burning, accidental ignition, fuel accumulation, and ordinary weather variability shape fire outcomes.
uncertainty: Component mechanisms and spatial overlap are supported, but event-by-event attribution to climate or warfare is absent.
compact_statement: Climate fire weather and warfare can compound wildfire risk through added ignition, explosive contamination, restricted access, and weakened suppression.

climate_pressure: Heat, flood, cold, and other climate pressures affecting displaced people and municipalities with changing populations
documented_impact: Unequal housing, health, water, education, social-protection, and emergency-service demand
fcv_mediator: War displacement, damaged housing, population and revenue change, uneven staffing, rural capacity gaps, and incomplete local integration
possible_consequence: Climate losses and recovery may become territorially unequal where frontline, host, return, rural, and smaller municipalities have different resources and needs
alternative_explanations: Pre-war territorial inequality, decentralization design, fiscal policy, economic geography, and demographic change affect municipal capacity independently.
uncertainty: Population and capacity differences are documented but not causally linked to climate outcomes across municipalities.
compact_statement: War displacement and uneven municipal capacity can make climate exposure, service pressure, and recovery highly unequal across places and groups.

climate_pressure: Reconstruction of war-damaged infrastructure and ecosystems under future heat, drought, flood, and water uncertainty
documented_impact: Decisions about energy, water, municipal assets, ecosystems, and community projects that can lock in or reduce future risk
fcv_mediator: Fragmented planning, finance and staffing gaps, uneven municipal participation, administrative burdens, inclusion failures, and shortened recovery timelines
possible_consequence: Climate-integrated and participatory recovery may strengthen resilience and legitimacy, while rushed or unequal investment may reproduce vulnerability and mistrust
alternative_explanations: Security conditions, donor requirements, macroeconomic constraints, legal reform, and ordinary project-management quality shape recovery outcomes.
uncertainty: Local evaluation and formal planning evidence do not establish national climate-resilience or peace effects.
compact_statement: Climate-informed, inclusive recovery can reduce lock-in, while fragmented or rushed investment may reproduce vulnerability, exclusion, and mistrust.
